reason: I'll start with the after-meal condition: the picture shows these cells releasing insulin into blood, which should help the muscle take in glucose.
expectation: I expect insulin to be released into the blood; the muscle storage may take another step.

alternatives.reason: The glucagon route also matches a goal, but I'll follow the after-meal sequence first.

effect: Insulin is now in the blood, ready to follow its route to muscle.
reaction: The route to muscle makes the next step clear.
reason: I'll follow the insulin message to the muscle to work toward storing glucose.
expectation: I expect the muscle to take in glucose and store some as carbohydrate, though I'm not sure exactly how the result will show it.

alternatives.reason: I could start the between-meals glucagon route, but I want to finish the insulin sequence first.

effect: Muscle has stored glucose, completing the insulin goal; the remaining route is glucagon.
reaction: Seeing insulin stay outside the cells makes its role as a message clearer.
reason: I'll follow the only available combination to start the between-meals glucagon goal.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic cells to release glucagon into the blood, with liver glucose release coming afterward.

effect: Glucagon is in the blood and can now carry the release message to the liver.
reaction: The route to the liver makes the next step clear.
reason: I'll follow the only available combination to release glucose from the liver's store.
expectation: I expect the liver to break down some stored carbohydrate and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver released glucose into the blood, completing the glucagon goal and showing how its store helps between meals.
reaction: The shrinking store made the result easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following insulin to muscle and glucagon to the liver was worthwhile because it made the contrast between storing and releasing glucose clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing glucagon was a fairly predictable repeat of releasing insulin, though it set up the comparison.

surprise.text: It was useful to see that insulin stays outside the muscle cells: it is a message, not part of the stored carbohydrate.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, but the compatible pairings and labels guided the actions; I did not work out how the signals operate in detail.

continue.text: I would consider another chapter if it connected different body systems in a similarly clear way, though I'd hope for more meaningful choices.
